problem:
Solve for $x$ in $Ax=b$ given that the matrix $A$ is orthogonal, and 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & -\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & 0 \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{5} \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$
worked_solution:
The inverse of an orthogonal matrix is equal to its transpose.

Hence, since $A$ is orthogonal, we have ${A}^{-1}={A}^{T}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax & =b \\ {A}^{-1}Ax & ={A}^{-1}b \\ x & ={A}^{-1}b \\ x & ={A}^{T}b \\ x & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & 0 \\ -\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\sqrt{5} \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\ x & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
